Question: What are the benefits of joining the military for culinary school?
Answer: The other answers are great and for the modern times. Here is an anecdote: During World War 2 my father was the lead officer of a mobile radar unit in the US Army from late 1942 until June of 1945. Towards the beginning of his command when they were in Northern Africa (prior to the invasion of Sicily and then fighting through Italy into Belgium and the Netherlands) he had a meeting with his master sergeant. “The soldiers are complaining about the food and our trucks are continually breaking down, call in the lead cook and the head of maintenance and lets figure out how to solve these issues” The head of maintenance came in and they spoke for several minutes, and then my Dad asked him: “What did you do in civilian life before you were drafted?” The soldier replied: “Sir, I was the head chef at the Waldorf Astoria in NY City”…….. Then they brought in the head cook. After a couple of minutes of discussion, my father asked the same question and the reply: “Sir, I was the head mechanic for a major trucking company” The US Army, when they drafted, didn’t always check to see where to assign the entering soldiers, but placed them into the open billets. My father then switched the roles of the two soldiers, never telling the upper commanders, and there were no more complaints about food nor maintenance for the next ~three years. There were complaints about getting shot-at in the front lines or going behind enemy lines to capture enemy radar systems…….

Question: How do you make your 8th grade basketball team? I’m average.
Answer: For the USA and someone in 8th grade at a middle school: Where I am, Massachusetts, middle school sports is generally for 8th grade students and possibly some advanced 7th graders. In MA, there is generally No Limit on how many players on the 8th grade team, and if they have too many, then they have two teams or possibly three teams. 8th grade team sports is supposed to be the place where you work on the skills necessary to make the JV team in high school. If there also is a freshman team at your high school, then that generally is open to all and will carry a large squad. When I say “open to all”, I mean: All of the players who have some “basic skills”, are willing to Try Hard to learn, and show up at Every practice and Every game (no matter what) unless excused by the coach. Since it is late July before US schools start their academic year, then you have ~4 months to “Whip your Basketball Butt into Shape”. You should be in the best athletic shape possible, and should know the basic rules of the sport, and be able to at least dribble with your dominant hand and also pass and shoot with that hand. Eventually you have to become ambidextrous to be a useful basketball player. Get out on the outdoor courts in your neighborhood and play as Much pick-up basketball that you can between now and tryouts in November. Good luck.

Question: Currently a third year university student, failed to get an internship last year, I want do a masters in finance and do an internship for my third year and for my masters, is this possible since most companies want 2nd year students for an intern?
Answer: First, speak with your professors (politely) and ask them if they can give you some assistance in finding an internship. It is best to find an internship near where you expect to spend the summer months, either remaining near the college for that summer (as our sons did during the summer prior to senior year in college) or get an internship near your “home” (if that is where you normally spend the summer), as one of our sons did the summer prior to junior year. Indeed, he got a business related internship with an engineering company that I was working with, so use All of your contacts to get an internship. Finally, speak with the head of your department. It may be possible to get a Co-Op paying job that includes your Spring term of junior year Plus the summer prior to senior year. I did that, putting together my own Co-Op program with the assistance of a professor and the head of my department. Good luck.

Question: Do school districts keep people in an IEP and speech therapy when they don't need to be in it just to make more money off them?
Answer: Make more money?????????????????????? Please stop the BAD JOKES. IEPs and special speech therapists COST money. And there are a cohort of students who need special 24x7 services that cost well over $120,000 per year when the typical school district (all expenses) spends ~$22,000 per student. About 18 years ago, my town had to raid its emergency funds for $750,000 because 7 students Suddenly needed 24x7 special education. And most of them were merely trying to escape their parents and by the time they were 18 years old, they were more than fine. A large percentage of the Special Ed and IEPs are scams. For those who Need it, it is life saving. However, there is always a cohort who will take illegal advantage of any situation. And all of that costs a Lot of money from the resident tax payers.
